name: Provider Data Mis-match — ANX.1 specialty Rx filed thru wrong state
description: Nine steps: identify the ANX event, confirm the provider is a specialty pharmacy, note the referring provider's Ancillary details and NPI, confirm the NPI against the claim image, search the provider database by NPI, find no match, and deny with PX_RANSRX.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.
steps.hint: Click the 'Event Resolution' tab. The Active Edit panel shows PX_ANX — 'SPECIALTY RX FILED THRU WRONG STATE'. The All Edits list below shows it among the claim's other events.
steps.name: Identify the ANX event
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab and look through the claim's edits for an ANX event. The ANX event means a specialty Rx claim may have been filed through the wrong state: it should have been filed with the plan where the REFERRING provider is located, and the referring provider is identified only by an NPI. Nothing on this tab tells you where that provider is. PX_ANX is present here, so work through the claim and establish it.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Provider Information tab.
steps.hint: Provider Info tab → Rendering section → Speciality description. It reads 'V13 – Pharmacy'.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the provider specialty is Pharmacy
steps.name: Verify the provider specialty is Pharmacy
steps.description: Before the specialty Rx filing rule is worth applying, establish that this is a claim it applies to. Open the Provider Information tab and read the Speciality description field in the Rendering section. It reads V13 – Pharmacy, so the provider is a specialty pharmacy and the rule is in scope.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens Claim Data → Details.
steps.hint: Claim Data tab → Details sub-tab → Additional Claim Data → Ancillary Provider. Type R, ZIP 12345, State NH.
steps.checklistItem: Note the referring provider's Ancillary details
steps.name: Note the referring provider's Ancillary details
steps.description: Open the Claim Data tab, then the Details sub-tab, and find the Ancillary Provider group inside Additional Claim Data. Note all three values: Type R, which marks these as the REFERRING physician's details, ZIP 12345 and State NH. They describe where the claim says the referring provider is, and the ANX event exists because that may not be where the provider actually is.

steps.completionTriggerNote: A deliberate return to the Provider Information tab, which step 2 already opened for the specialty. The trainee must go back to it while this step is active.
steps.hint: Provider Info tab → Referring section → NPI. It reads 12345678910.
steps.name: Note the referring provider NPI
steps.description: Go back to the Provider Information tab, this time for the Referring section. The NPI field reads 12345678910. This is the only identifier the claim carries for the referring provider, and everything that follows depends on it.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Claim Image tab.
steps.hint: Claim Image tab → Claim Image – Provider Information → Referring → 17b. NPI. It matches the claim record: 12345678910.
steps.checklistItem: Compare the NPI against the claim image
steps.name: Compare the NPI against the claim image
steps.description: The claim record is only a keyed-in copy of the form the provider submitted, so check the NPI against the form itself. Open the Claim Image tab and read field 17b in the Referring group of the Claim Image – Provider Information block. It shows 12345678910, the same NPI the claim record carries. The NPI is present and correctly keyed, so there is no keying error to fix — the question is who that NPI belongs to and where they are.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens Search → Provider. Opening the sub-tab completes this step only; the Search press completes step 7.
steps.hint: Search tab → Provider sub-tab. The form arrives empty, with Source system on SPS.
steps.name: Open the provider search
steps.description: To find out where the referring provider is, look them up in the provider database. Open the Search tab, then the Provider sub-tab. The filter boxes are empty and the Source system is already set to SPS. Nothing is searched yet.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Search press passes the action's guard: the NPI box must hold 12345678910, Source system must be SPS, and no other filter box may carry a value. The From and Through dates may be filled or left empty either way.
steps.hint: Enter 12345678910 in the NPI box, leave Source system on SPS and the other boxes empty, and click Search. The result reads 'No matching records found with the given search criteria'.
steps.checklistItem: Search by NPI and check the NPI Registry
steps.name: Search by NPI and check the NPI Registry
steps.description: Type the referring provider's NPI, 12345678910, into the NPI box and click Search. Leave Source system on SPS and every other filter box empty; the From and Through dates may be filled or left blank. The search returns no matching records with the given search criteria, so the referring provider is not in our database. The next step in the live system would be the NPPES NPI Registry at https://nppes.cms.hhs.gov/NPPESRegistry/NPIRegistrySearch.do?subAction=reset&searchType=ind — enter the NPI in the NPI Number field, click Search and review the provider details and address. In this application the NPI Registry is not accessed, and no matching record is found there either. The correct address cannot be determined, so the claim is rejected.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Deny Claim panel (which dispatches the deny_claim action).
steps.hint: Action menu → Deny claim. Enter reject code PX_RANSRX in the Deny Claim section, click Submit, then confirm the pop-up.
steps.checklistItem: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_RANSRX
steps.name: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_RANSRX
steps.description: The referring provider is in neither the provider database nor the NPI Registry, so the correct address to use on the claim cannot be determined and the claim cannot be routed to the right plan. From the Action menu select Deny claim. A Deny Claim section appears below the header. Enter reject code PX_RANSRX in the input box — the matching code appears in a dropdown list — select it and click Submit.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits Deny from the header Decision dropdown.
steps.name: Submit Deny decision
steps.description: Record the outcome on the claim. In the Decision section of the header, select Deny from the dropdown and click Submit.
